title: $\texttt{NOCE-Net}$: Representation Learning for Battery Operational Context via Nested Sequence Modelling
claim: Raw sequential data is restructured into nested units, then a hierarchical encoder with a recurrent backbone learns state representations by predicting responses.
layout: 2 stacked dashed panels, left-to-right flow, nested stage-2 diagram with colored module regions
description: The figure has two dashed-border panels stacked vertically. Stage 1 (top) shows a raw operational context sequence u1–u9 with a matching voltage response sequence v1–v9, both cut into three Full Equivalent Cycles (FEC 1–3). An arrow runs through a re-BatteryData box to the segmented outputs U1, U2 and U3. Stage 2 (bottom) shows the NOCE-Net architecture. A blue Patch Encoder region holds the metadata, MPE and FEC embeddings. An orange Recurrent Backbone column stacks three GRU cells with hidden states h1–h3. A purple Patch Decoder region contains a transformer encoder and an output reconstruction layer. An initialization pathway sits at the top left. Green output bars show the predicted voltages V1–V3. Colored arrows (black, orange, purple, green) carry the data flow. The eye goes first to the Stage 1 sequence strips, then to the central GRU column.
caption: Two-stage pipeline: re-BatteryData converts raw aging data into nested operational context, which is a bi-level sequence representation of battery data with the outer sequence representing equivalent cycles and the inner sequence corresponding to each equivalent cycle representing the finer inputs during each cycle. (Stage 1); NOCE-Net learns representations via voltage response prediction based on the nested operational context representation and learns health-indicating latents without explicit training to learn degradation (Stage 2). Abbreviations: Tran. Enc. = Transformer Encoder, MPE = Multi-Patch Embedding, ORL = Output Reconstruction Layer, GRU = Gated Recurrent Unit.
abstract: Learning effective representations from battery operational history is essential for predictive health management and control-oriented applications. Existing approaches rely on response-dependent engineered features or short early-life windows, limiting generalisability and precluding use in prospective settings where future responses are unavailable. We propose NOCE-Net, a deep nested sequence model that learns control-enabling representations directly from raw cyclic operational or telemetric data. Our data pipeline, re-BatteryData, standardises heterogeneous aging datasets into semantically equivalent Full Equivalent Cycles (FECs) defined by absolute charge throughput, enabling end-to-end learning across diverse operational regimes. NOCE-Net combines multi-patch transformer encoders for intra-cycle dynamics with a GRU backbone for inter-cycle state evolution, operating on approximately $700$ batteries across ten public datasets spanning over $300$ operational profiles. In zero-shot evaluation on unseen battery chemistries and usage patterns, NOCE-Net achieves $13.7\%$ MAPE in voltage response prediction, outperforming strong long-sequence baselines by over $43\%$ while using $40 \times$ fewer parameters. Shape and component diagnostics of the learned hidden states reveal that the GRU's principal direction of evolution achieves Spearman $|Ï| \geq 0.95$ with the capacity fade trajectory on average across all datasets with monotone degradation profiles, including zero-shot test batteries, providing evidence that the representations encode degradation dynamics transferable to downstream tasks beyond battery response modelling. Code is available at https://github.com/BeArnab96/NOCE-Net.
